text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Austrian President Thomas Klestil says 1997 will be a year of reforms, says there is no time for arguments in the goverment coalition.

- Chancellor Franz Vranitzky tells the paper he has no intentions to become Austrian president when Klestil's mandate runs out in 1998, but says his Social Democrats will nominate their own candidate to compete against Klestil should he decide to run for a second term.
- Around 135,000 revellers braved sub-zero temperatures to greet the new year on the streets of Vienna's historic city centre.
- Some 261,000 Austrians were without a job at the end of the year, slightly more than a year ago.
- Far-right leader Joerg Haider signals he may support an initiative by the conservative People's Party to sell the state's stake in Creditanstalt on the Vienna bourse.
- Defence Minister Werner Fasslabend says he wants more funds to buy new fighter jets for Austria's army.
- Generali-led consortium of bidders for Creditanstalt may team up with rival bidder Karl Wlaschek to bid for state's stake in flagship bank against market leader Bank Austria.
- President Klestil vows he will not be curtailed in his official duties as a consequence of his recent pneumonia.
- Chancellor Franz Vranitzky says 1997 should be a year without nationwide elections.
